beats.narration_text: Hi, I'm Dhruvi Mehta, and this is my final project pitch: Ghost-Job Trust Radar. If something already ran, I'll show it. Everything else is a plan.

show.event: types 'Is this job worth applying to?'
backspaces 'worth applying to' and retypes 'live and CPT-feasible'

props.text: Is this job worth applying to?

beats.motion_claim: CONSTRUCTED. The writer types the naive question and corrects it to 'live and CPT-feasible'.

qc.sparse_reason: Hesitant-writer bookend: the correction is the motion.

beats.narration_text: Four terms. CPT: work authorization tied to a degree program. A ghost job: a posting that's already filled, or never really open. Liveness: whether it still accepts applications. A sponsorship record: a public filing showing a company sponsored a visa before.

a public filing showing a company sponsored a visa before

qc.sparse_reason: TERMS card: four prerequisites, one line each.

beats.narration_text: An international student on CPT finds a data analyst posting and spends an hour researching the company. Then she learns it was already filled, or the start date doesn't fit her CPT window. That hour is gone.

shot.visual_intent: CONSTRUCTED. A posting box on a desk; browser tabs stack up beside it; then the posting box greys out. Labels: 'Posting', '1 hour'.

beats.narration_text: Ghost-Job Trust Radar will be a command-line tool that checks the posting first. Is it live? Does the timeline fit CPT? Is there a sponsorship record? The finished artifact will be a GitHub repository with one command, tests, and an evaluation log.

shot.visual_intent: CONSTRUCTED. A conveyor carries the posting box through three gates into a report. Labels: 'Live?', 'CPT fit?', 'Sponsor record?'.
shot.motion_claim: CONSTRUCTED. A conveyor carries the posting box through three gates into a report. Labels: 'Live?', 'CPT fit?', 'Sponsor record?'.

beats.narration_text: I looked at two alternatives. MyVisaJobs shows who sponsored before, but nothing I saw checks whether a posting is live or fits a CPT window. The manual checklist from career guides works, but it's four or five steps across tabs, with no record kept.

shot.visual_intent: CONSTRUCTED. Two stations: a database cabinet and a desk of scattered tabs. Labels: 'MyVisaJobs', 'Manual check'.

beats.narration_text: Mine will check liveness first and stop if the posting is dead, before research starts. Every value will carry its source. If the data has nothing, it will say 'no record in this dataset,' never 'doesn't sponsor.'

shot.visual_intent: CONSTRUCTED. The conveyor again; the first gate turns red and the later gates go dim. Then a report box with a tag. Labels: 'Stop early', 'No record'.

beats.narration_text: My reader is a hiring manager for a data analyst role. In sixty seconds, they'll open the README, run one command on a sample posting, and see every line's source. This picture is a mock-up.

beats.narration_text: Here's what exists. Last assignment, I built a CPT timeline gate and a sponsorship-data builder. This is the real test run: sixteen offline tests pass. I also checked one run by hand against the raw data.
beats.motion_claim: REAL. The lens moves down the two real test lines from the 2026-10-10 run to the total, 16.

beats.narration_text: Then I tried to break it, with a company that isn't in the dataset. It reported 'no record' instead of inventing an answer.

beats.narration_text: It will show four course skills: verification, source grounding, evaluation, and prompt contracts. A reviewer could fairly conclude I build checks that fail safely, but not that it's accurate on real postings. That isn't tested yet.

beats.narration_text: What's out: it won't tell anyone whether to apply, and it won't give legal or immigration advice. First, I'll make one command run every check on a synthetic posting. You'll know it ran because it writes a report, a test checks it, and a dated run log goes in the repo.

shot.visual_intent: CONSTRUCTED. A crossed-out 'apply?' sign, then one command running a single synthetic posting into a report and a log. Labels: 'Not advice', 'First run'.

beats.narration_text: The biggest risk: the sponsorship data is an incomplete historical sample, so someone could read 'no record' as 'doesn't sponsor.' So every lookup will print the dataset's date range next to the answer.

beats.narration_text: Why this project? It's a real problem for international students like me, and it's a mix: Python and data cleaning I already have, with last assignment's scripts as evidence. Prompt contracts and evaluation logs are new to me.

shot.visual_intent: CONSTRUCTED. Two shelves: one with tools I already have, one with new boxes being added. Labels: 'Already have', 'Learning'.

beats.narration_text: So, where things stand. Today: a recipe, two scripts, sixteen passing tests, and a break test, in an open pull request not yet reviewed. The single command, live check, and evaluation log come later. This film does not establish that the tool works on real postings.
beats.motion_claim: CONSTRUCTED. The tab switches from what exists today to what will exist.

beats.narration_text: Your turn. Before researching your next posting: is it still accepting applications, and does the start date fit your work window? Note where each answer came from.
